title: Op Amp Performance and One-Stage Op Amps
intro: An operational amplifier is a high-gain differential amplifier designed to be used in feedback. The specifications decide the topology.

items: Gain (open-loop, DC): 40 to 100+ dB, set by gm*ro stages.
Small-signal bandwidth and unity-gain frequency (GBW), as in the frequency chapter.
Large-signal behaviour: slew rate and output swing.
Linearity, noise, input offset (random mismatch, plus systematic).
CMRR and PSRR: rejection of common-mode and supply variations.
Telescopic cascode: highest gain (about (gm*ro)^2/2), lowest noise and power, fast, but smallest swing and an input common-mode range that must sit high.
Folded cascode: the input pair and the cascode have opposite polarity so the input common-mode range can include the supply or ground; more current and noise, but wider swing.
Basic five-transistor OTA with active load: gain only gm*(ro||ro) (25 to 50), the simplest and best-behaved.
Gain of cascode stage: Av = gm1 * Rout where Rout is the parallel of the two cascode output resistances.

blocks.text: Pick the load capacitance and the required GBW to find gm1 = 2*pi*GBW*CL. The current for each device follows from gm and Vov. Check swing, then gain. If gain falls short, increase L or switch to a cascode.

blocks.title: Folded-cascode gain
blocks.text: gm1 = 2 mS. The output resistance looking into the NMOS cascode branch is 3 Mohm and into the PMOS cascode branch is 3 Mohm. Find the gain.
solution: Av = gm1 * Rout = 2 mS * 1.5 Mohm = 3000, or 69.5 dB.

blocks.title: Sizing for bandwidth
blocks.text: A single-stage op amp must have GBW = 100 MHz driving CL = 1 pF. What gm does the input pair need? If Vov = 0.15 V, what current per side?
solution: ID = gm * Vov / 2 = 0.628 mS * 0.15 V / 2 = 47 uA per side (about 94 uA for the pair).
blocks.answer: gm = 0.63 mS, ID = 47 uA per side.
